UPSTREAM: ASoC: Intel: Fix nested/unnecessary Kconfig dependencies This patch fixes a number of issues: 1. IOSF_MBI is only needed for byt-cr detection, which is only supported on Baytrail/Cherrytrail, move to HiFi2 config 2. SND_SOC_INTEL_SST should not select SND_SOC_INTEL_SST_ACPI, the latter config is only valid for Haswell/Baytrail legacy but not needed by Skylake 3. SND_SST_IPC_ACPI, used only by the atom/sst driver, should not select SND_SOC_INTEL_SST, none of the code under common/sst*.c is used This nesting of configs really makes no sense, it's easier to maintain if for each platform one can control what is strictly required. Compiled-tested with each of Haswell, Baytrail legacy, HiFi2, SKL cases selected independently. 0-day and explicit randconfig tests did not report additional issues and no functionality loss was observed in Intel tests on HIFI2 and SKYLAKE platforms Signed-off-by: Pierre-Louis Bossart <pierre-louis.bossart@linux.intel.com> Reviewed-by: Andy Shevchenko <andriy.shevchenko@linux.intel.com> Acked-By: Vinod Koul <vinod.koul@intel.com> Signed-off-by: Mark Brown <broonie@kernel.org> (cherry picked from commit f3f2bb7a0ebf9d83229810f69a53fee2c0441b2c) Signed-off-by: Samaga Prasanna Krishna <samaga.krishna@intel.corp-partner.google.com> BUG=b:110025789 TEST=Test Audio use cases after full SOF series patches are applied. FROMGIT: ath10k: allocate small size dma memory in ath10k_pci_diag_write_mem ath10k_pci_diag_write_mem may allocate big size of the dma memory based on the parameter nbytes. Take firmware diag download as example, the biggest size is about 500K. In some systems, the allocation is likely to fail because it can't acquire such a large contiguous dma memory. The fix is to allocate a small size dma memory. In the loop, driver copies the data to the allocated dma memory and writes to the destination until all the data is written. Tested with QCA6174 PCI with firmware-6.bin_WLAN.RM.4.4.1-00119-QCARMSWP-1, this also affects QCA9377 PCI. Signed-off-by: Carl Huang <cjhuang@codeaurora.org> Reviewed-by: Brian Norris <briannorris@chomium.org> Signed-off-by: Kalle Valo <kvalo@codeaurora.org> (cherry picked from commit 0738b4998c6d1caf9ca2447b946709a7278c70f1 git://git.kernel.org/pub/scm/linux/kernel/git/kvalo/ath.git ath-next) BUG=b:70048735 TEST=wifi_matfunc, suspend/resume on QCA6174A Change-Id: I4d7547dcf518f5d2a481d8b9171b152e3c4c7113 Signed-off-by: Brian Norris <briannorris@chromium.org> Reviewed-on: https://chromium-review.googlesource.com/1285557

servod ec3po: Use os.pipe() pipes for StartLoop() shutdown_pipe args. For StartLoop() shutdown_pipe arguments, this replaces use of threadproc.Pipe() i.e. multiprocessing.Pipe() pipes with os.pipe()-based file objects. This divorce from the other uses of of threadproc.Pipe() is necessary because the post-threading transition plan for the latter will have them move away from the pipe idiom entirely. The shutdown_pipe functionality must use pipes because they exist to interrupt blocked select/poll/epoll on the raw UARTs without using signals. The other uses of threadproc.Pipe() will migrate away from pipes to a more direct inter-thread synchronization mechanism, in order to avoid the Python object serialization and deserialization that will no longer be necessary once ec3po is in a single process. BRANCH=none BUG=b:79684405 TEST=With a servo_micro connected to an octopus_ite, functionality involving the EC console continues to work. I tested dut-control ec_uart_pty (including using the UART with minicom), dut_i2c_mux, get_ite_chipid commands. Additionally, servod shutdown via either ctrl+c or SIGTERM still happens correctly, without any delay, leftover processes, or tracebacks. Change-Id: I8bc1759672227bc7f65359cb3f9fc7d8e09f7a91 Signed-off-by: Matthew Blecker <matthewb@chromium.org> Reviewed-on: https://chromium-review.googlesource.com/1281997 Tested-by: Ruben Rodriguez Buchillon <coconutruben@chromium.org> Reviewed-by: Ruben Rodriguez Buchillon <coconutruben@chromium.org>
